source - Section 197 has been amended by Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 with effect from 1-9-2019 to provide that a certificate for lower or 'nil' deduction may also be issued for section 194M [see para 12.8]. Accordingly, the AO shall give such certificate on receipt of an application from the payee and after being satisfied that the total income of such person justifies no TDS or TDS at lower rates. 12.5-2m Whether tax is deductible on GST component? - The CBDT has clarified by issuing Circulars from time to time that tax is not required to be deducted on Service tax/GST component [Circular No. 4/2008, dated 28-4-2008, Circular No. 1/2014, dated 13-1-2014, Circular No.23/2017 dated 19-7-2017]. Rajasthan High Court has held that tax is not required to be deducted in such cases [CIT (TDS) Jaipur v. Rajasthan Urban Infrastructure [2013] 37 taxmann.com 154/218 Taxman 10 (Mag.) (Raj.)]. Hence, it can be said that tax is not required to be deducted on GST component, if the amount of consideration and GST are separately reflected in the Tax invoice.

12.5-2n Credit of TDS - When? - As per the provision of section 198(1), tax deducted in accordance with Chapter XVII-B is treated as deemed income of the payee or the recipient. Section 199(1) provides that tax deducted under the Chapter XVII-B would be treated as payment of tax on behalf of the payee. Further, rule 37BA(3)(i) provides that the credit of such TDS shall be given for the assessment year in which such income is assessable.

Thus, credit of TDS deducted under the section would be available only in the year in which the income is offered to tax by the payee. It may take time to complete work. Therefore, in order to avoid hardship of getting tax credit in future, it is advisable that the payee should:

keep and preserve the TDS certificate(s) issued by the tax deductor; or

keep tracking records of Form 26AS on Government website; or

download Form 26AS and preserve the soft copy.

12.5-2-o Other consequences in case of default - If the person responsible to deduct tax under the section fails to deduct or after deducting fails to deposit the tax, there could be consequences, like, liability to interest, penalty or prosecution under the Act.

INTEREST & PENALTY

Mandatory and automatic - The interest is to compensate the revenue for the loss which it has suffered on account of late receipt of the tax. Thus, provisions of interest u/s 201 are mandatory and automatic and interest has to be paid from date on which tax was deductible till date on which tax is actually paid [CIT v. Rathi Gum Industries [1995] 213 ITR 98 (Raj.)].

Even if assessee was bona fide in not making such deduction, it was liable to pay interest [Sun Outsourcing Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2018] 92 taxmann.com 339 (AP)].

Interest u/s 201(1A) is leviable even where recipient is a loss-making company [CIT v. Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board [2011] 14 taxmann.com 73/202 Taxman 454 (Mad.)]. Also see, CIT v. Punjab Infrastructure Dev. Board [2016] 76 taxmann.com 365/[2017] 245 Taxman 183 (P&H), SLP granted inPunjab Infrastructure Dev Board v. CIT [2019] 102 taxmann.com 224/261 Taxman 249 (SC).

Where tax has already been paid by deductee, no further tax can be collected by deductor, however, interest can be charged from deductor from date of its liability till date of actual tax payment by deductee [S. A. A. Ispahani Trust v. ITO [2013] 34 taxmann.com 29/216 Taxman 1 (Mad.)].

Interest u/s 201(1A) for belated remittance of tax deducted at source on dividend must be calculated with reference to date of issue of dividend warrants, and not with reference to date of declaration of dividend [CIT v. Hindustan General Industries Ltd. [2000] 113 Taxman 506 (Delhi)].

Assessee's liability to pay interest u/s 201(1A) would end on date when such tax has been deposited by recipient, either by way of advance tax or along with return of income [CIT v. Bharat Hotels Ltd. [2015] 64 taxmann.com 325 (Kar.)].

Certificates issued by Central Government Departments - TDS certificates issued by Central Government Departments should be accepted by Assessing Officers if they indicate that credit has been afforded to the Income-tax Department by book adjustment, and the date of such book adjustment is indicated therein. The certificate, in any case, should be genuine. In case of doubt about genuineness of such TDS certificates, the Assessing Officers are free to correspond with the DDOs of such Central Government departments and the latter are bound to offer facility for examination of their payments made to Central Government account by book adjustment. Further, all such DDOs issuing certificates where credit is shown by book adjustment must obtain a TAN (Tax Account Number) from the jurisdictional I.T. authority/Officer-in-charge of TDS matters, and must also file their Annual Return of TDS to the jurisdictional officer-in-charge of TDS. The TAN must be quoted on the TDS certificates issued, showing payment by book adjustment - Circular : No. 749, dated 27-12-1996.

Issue of certificate is mandatory - Issue of certificate for tax deduction at source under section 203 is mandatory in all cases where tax is deducted at source, including cases where payments are made 'net of tax' in terms of section 195A.—Circular : No. 785, dated 24-11-1999.

Issue of TDS Certificate in cases of Truck/Goods-carriage Operators - Representations have been received that in the case of the road transporters, where tax is deducted under section 194C from the payment being made to the truck-operator on delivery of the goods by the consignee, the certificate is either not being issued by the consignee within the prescribed time or the certificate is being issued in favour of the consignor of the goods at the place of the truck-operator. As a result of such irregularities, the truck-operator is not able to claim credit for the tax deducted from the payments received by him.

In consideration of the above and the trade-practice prevailing in the road-transport industry, where the truck or such other goods carriages is booked by the consignor but the payment is made by the consignee on delivery of the goods, the Board hereby reiterates the provisions of section 203, and advises the consignee to issue TDS certificate in the cases of the truck/goods-carriage operators within the prescribed time and in favour of such truck/goods-carriage operators.

It may be clarified in this regard that in case of any failure in timely issue of certificate or in case of issue of certificate in favour of any person other than the person from whose payment tax has been deducted at source, the provisions of section 272A(2)(g) shall be attracted, under which, penalty of one hundred rupees for every day during which the failure continues is leviable—Circular : No. 6/2006, dated 23-6-2006.

8.4-5 Credit for the tax deducted or collected - The provision in relation to :—

TDS [section 199(3)], reads as follows: "where any deduction is made. . . on or after the 1st day of April, 2005 and paid to the Central Government, the amount of tax deducted and specified in the statement referred to in section 203AA shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the person referred to in sub-section (1)... and credit shall be given to him for the amount so deducted in the assessment... without production of certificate." (Emphasis supplied)

TCS [first proviso to section 206C(4)] reads: "provided that where any amount is collected... on or after 1st day of April, 2005 and paid... to the credit of the Central Government, the amount of tax collected and specified in statement referred to... shall be deemed as payment of tax on behalf of the person from whom the amount has been collected and credit shall be given to him for the amount so collected in the assessment... without production of certificate." (Emphasis supplied)

Thus, the amount of tax deducted/collected and specified in the Statement would be treated as tax paid on behalf of the payee/buyer. It appears, the payee/buyer would get credit for such tax deducted/collected on his/her behalf. For whatever reasons, the amount of tax deducted/collected is not specified in the Statement, the amount not specified would not be treated as tax deducted/collected on behalf of the payee/buyer and credit will not be available for the same to the payee/buyer.

In this connection an issue may arise about the treatment of tax deducted or collected and specified in the statement but not paid by the payer/collector. If appears that to the extent tax deducted/collected, whether specified in the statement or not the recovery cannot be enforced against the payee/buyer, for the following reasons :

Section 203AA and second proviso to section 206C(5), respectively provide that the prescribed income-tax authorities or authorised person shall prepare and collect the statement of tax deducted/paid [under section 192(1A)] on tax collected.

(ii)

Section 199(3) and first proviso to section 206C(4) treat the tax deducted or collected and specified in the statement as tax paid on behalf of the payee or buyer. Thus, the tax deducted on collected, whether paid or not is the relevant amount which can be considered as paid on behalf of the payee/buyer.

(ii)

Section 205 of the Act provides that where the tax is deductible at source under applicable provisions of Chapter XVII, the assessee shall not be called upon to pay the tax to the extent to which tax has been deducted from that income;

(iii)

Section 191 contemplates direct payment by the payee only in a case where tax is deducted in terms of Chapter XVII and not in a case where the tax is deducted and not paid.

GENERAL

Constitutional validity - Section 201 is a penal provision to treat a person as an assessee-in-default if there is a failure to deduct the tax or to pay the tax after it is deducted. Sufficient safeguards have been provided in the section itself, and as such it cannot be considered that the provisions are ultra vires the Constitution [Mittal Steel Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [1999] 240 ITR 707 (Kar.)].

ASSESSEE-IN-DEFAULT

Competent authority - In terms of section 201, it is assessing authority who is competent person to pass an order holding an assessee to be 'assessee-in-default' and not Director General (Systems) [CIT v. Kingfisher Airlines Ltd. [2014] 49 taxmann.com 49 (Kar.)].

AO couldn't treat payer as assessee-in-default without examining his submission justifying non-deduction of tax [Remco (BHEL) House Building Co-Operative Society Ltd. v. ITO [2015] 58 taxmann.com 317/232 Taxman 355 (Kar.)].

AO has jurisdiction to demand amount of tax not deducted at source by an order passed u/s 201(1) and 201(1A). If assessee takes defence that payee has paid tax on money, it is for him to prove it; AO is not obliged to explore possible defences and to collect evidence in support thereof [Nopany Marketing Co. (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 57 taxmann.com 186/231 Taxman 802 (Cal.)].

No demand notice required - By virtue of provisions u/s 201, a person is deemed to be an 'assessee-in-default' in view of statutory provision contained therein and in such a case, there is no scope of giving further notice of demand u/s 156 which is applicable only in cases when any tax, interest, penalty, fine or any other sum is payable in consequence of any order passed under the 1961 Act. Thus, in a case where section 201(1) is attracted there is no need of giving any notice u/s 156 and if any such notice is given the same should be held to be redundant [PILCOM v. CIT [2011] 11 taxmann.com 103 (Cal.)].

Section 191 vis-à-vis section 201 - The language of the Explanation to section 191 and section 201(1) is almost similar except with one difference. In the former section, the deductor shall be deemed to be an assessee-in-default where the assessee has also failed to pay such tax directly, whereas in section 201(1), this condition is not mentioned. While interpreting the provisions of sections 191 and 201(1), a harmonious construction has to be adopted and such interpretation is to be put which gives meaning and purpose to both the provisions. Explanation to section 191 specifically mentions "....be deemed to be an assessee in default within the meaning of section 201(1) in respect of such tax". The above meaning, thus, has to be read in section 201(1), which has been specifically provided for. Not repeating the said condition again in section 201(1) is inconsequential. Thus, the deductor who fails to deduct TDS shall be deemed to be an assessee-in-default only when the assessee has also failed to pay such tax directly. Thus, it flows that there is no occasion to treat the deductor as an assessee-in-default unless the assessee has not paid the tax directly [Jagran Prakashan Ltd. v. DCIT [2012] 21 taxmann.com 489/209 Taxman 92 (All.)].

Assessee not in default - There is nothing in section 201 to treat the employer as the defaulter where there is a shortfall in the deduction of tax at source. The expression 'as required by or under the Act' grammatically refers only to the duty to pay the tax that is deducted and cannot refer to the duty to deduct the tax. If there is any shortfall due to any difference of opinion as to the taxability of any item, the employer cannot be declared to be an assessee-in-default [P. V. Rajagopal v. UOI [1998] 99 Taxman 475 (AP)]. Also see, CIT v. Sony India (P.) Ltd. [2012] 17 taxmann.com 126/210 Taxman 55 (Kar.).

Reimbursement - Self-certification by employees that they had incurred expenditure towards uniform was sufficient for assessee employer not to deduct TDS on reimbursement made by it to said employees towards such expenditure incurred by them [CIT v. Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Ltd. [2020] 122 taxmann.com 159/[2021] 277 Taxman 284 (Guj.)]. Adjustment of TDS deduction available - If there is a failure to deduct in a FY, the same can be deducted by way of adjustment during the same FY. In such a case, the obligation to deduct stands extended up to the end of the FY. But the right to adjustment does not extend beyond FY [CIT v. Enron Expat Services Inc. [2010] 194 Taxman 70 (Uttarakhand)].

Estimated income - A duty is cast on an employer to form an opinion about the tax liability of his employee in respect of the salary income. While forming this opinion, the employer is undoubtedly expected to act honestly and fairly. But if it is found that the estimate made by the employer is incorrect, this fact alone, without anything more, would not inevitably lead to the inference that the employer has not acted honestly and fairly. Unless that inference can be reasonably raised against an employer, no fault can be found with him [Gwalior Rayon Silk Co. Ltd. v. CIT [1983] 14 Taxman 99 (MP); CIT v. Delhi Public School [2011] 15 taxmann.com 107/203 Taxman 81 (Delhi)].

The rates to tax and the estimate of income will have to be calculated on annual basis and whatever is to be included under the head "Salaries" will have to be taken into consideration for the purpose of making this estimate [British Airways v. CIT [1991] 54 Taxman 470 (Cal.)].

Merely because the employee gives in writing that he will make the savings of particular amount, then TDS should also be reduced proportionately while estimating the salary, so that it may not result in hardship to the incumbent that he may have to pay income-tax in lump sum at the end of FY from his salary, is impracticable as per the Income-tax Act [Major General Vinay Kumar Singh v. UOI [2002] 123 Taxman 750 (MP)].

Performance incentive - Performance incentive cannot be a fixed mandatory payment made year after year. Since it is dependent on the performance of the company in a given FY, the payment of such incentive is not only uncertain but the amount is also likely to vary, therefore, employer held not accountable for short deduction of TDS to the extent income relates to performance incentive [CIT v. Marubeni India (P.) Ltd. [2007] 165 Taxman 467 (Delhi)].

Stay on TDS deduction - Where assessee-employer was prevented by interim order of Court from deducting tax on salary of its employees, assessee could not be deemed to be an assessee-in-default for period interim order was in force [Regional Dir. ONGC Ltd. v. Assn. of Sc. & Tech. Offr. ONGC Ltd. [2012] 27 taxmann.com 222/211 Taxman 593 (SC)].

Section 199

Finance Act, 2008

Credit for tax deducted at source - Amendment to section 199 regarding credit for tax deducted

8.4 Section 199, prior to the amendment by the Finance Act, 2008, provided that any deduction of tax at source made under Chapter XVII and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, or of the owner of the security, or depositor or owner of property or of a unit holder or the shareholder, as the case may be. It was provided that credit shall be given to such person for the amount so deducted on the production of the certificate furnished under section 203 and such credit would be given in the assessment for the assessment year in which such income is assessable. The provisos to section 199(1) provided that

in cases where certain income was included in the total income of a person under section 60 (transfer of income without transfer of asset), section 61 (revocable transfer), section 64 (clubbing), section 93 (transfer of income of non-residents), section 94 (transactions in securities), the credit shall be given to the person in whose hands such income is taxable;

In case dividend income was assessable as an income of a person other than the shareholders, the credit shall be given to such other person in such circumstances as may be prescribed; and

If a property or asset is owned jointly by two or more persons not constituting a partnership, the credit shall be given to each such person in the same proportion in which such income is assessable as his income.

Section 199(2) provided that any tax paid under section 192(1A) shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the employee and credit shall be given to him for the amount so deducted on the production of the certificate under section 203 in the assessment year in which such income is assessable.

Section 199(3) provided that in respect of any tax deduction made on or after 1-4-2008 and paid to the Central Government, the amount of tax deducted and specified in the statement referred to in section 203AA shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the persons referred to in section 199(1)/(2) and credit shall be given to him for the amounts so deducted in the assessment for which income is assessable without the production of certificates.

The Finance Act, 2008 has substituted, with effect from 1-4-2008, the aforesaid section as follows :

Sub-section (1) provides that any deduction made in accordance with Chapter XVII and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, or of the owner of the security, or of the depositor or of the owner of property or of the unitholder, or of the shareholder, as the case may be.

Sub-section (2) provides that any sum referred to in section 192(1A) and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as the tax paid on behalf of the person in respect of whose income such payment of tax has been made.

Sub-section (3) provides that the Board may, for the purposes of giving credit in respect of tax deducted or tax paid in terms of the provisions of this Chapter, make the following rules:

(a)

rules for the purposes of giving credit to a person other than those referred to in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2),

(b)

rules for the assessment year for which such credit may be given, and

(c)

such other rules as may be necessary.

Thus, the gist of the amendment is that (a) the power to give credit to a person other than the person in whose name deduction has been made is now given to the Board instead of stating such instances in the Act itself; and (b) the Board will now also have the power to prescribe rules for the assessment year for which the credit of tax may be given and the manner in which such credit shall be given.

Finance Act, 2002

Amendment of rectification provisions for credit for tax deduction at source [Section 155]

9.5 Under section 199, any deduction of tax at source in accordance with the provisions of sections 192 to 196D and paid to the account of Central Government is treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, and credit is given to such person for the amounts so deducted on the production of a certificate furnished under section 203 in the assessment year for which such income is assessable.

In many cases certificates under section 203 are not furnished to the payee and as a result credit is not given for the tax so deducted.

With a view to mitigate this hardship, section 155(14), has been inserted, with effect from 1-6-2002, to provide that where in the assessment under section 143(3) or in any intimation or deemed intimation under section 143(1), credit for tax deducted has not been given under section 199 on the ground that the certificate furnished under section 203 was not filed with the return and subsequently such certificate is produced before the Assessing Officer within two years from the end of the assessment year in which such income is assessable, credit of tax deducted at source shall be given to the assessee on production of such certificate by rectification of the assessment order/intimation/deemed intimation. However, such rectification shall be made only if the income from which tax has been deducted has been disclosed in the return of income filed by the assessee for that assessment year [proviso to section 155(14)].

The time limit for rectification is 2 years from the end of the assessment year in which the income is assessable. Hence, in case of scrutiny assessments for which the same time limit is provided, the amendment does not provide any significant time for rectification after such assessment is complete.

8.2 Allowing credit of all TDS & TCS in computing TDS from salary income [Section 192]

8.2-1 Pre-amended provision

Section 192 of the Act provides for the deduction of tax at source on salary income. Sub-section (2B) of Section 192 provides that employees can furnish to their employers the details of their income under any other head and the tax, if any, deducted thereon to be taken into account for the purposes of calculating the tax to be deducted under this provision from the salary income.

Where an employee has also suffered any loss under the head house property, the employer shall take such loss into account to calculate the tax liability, provided supporting evidence/proof has been provided by the employee. After receiving details of other income from the employee, the employer shall calculate the amount of tax to be deducted from his monthly salary income.

8.2-2 Amendments by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024

The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 has amended sub-section (2B) of Section 192 to allow the employer to consider any tax deducted or collected under the provisions of Part B or Part BB of Chapter XVII of the Act. Previously, only the TDS related to the income that the employee intimated to the employer was considered while computing TDS under Section 192.

Further, the proviso to Section 192(2B) has been substituted, which provides as follows:

"Provided that this sub-section shall not in any case have the effect of reducing the tax deductible from income under the head "salaries" except where the loss under the head "Income from house property" and the tax deducted in accordance with other provisions of Part B and collected in accordance with the provisions of Part BB, of this Chapter, has been taken into account"

The amendment is effective from 1-10- 2024.

8.2-2a The rationale behind the amendment - In recent years, the scope of TCS has been substantially expanded to various transactions, such as the purchase of motor cars, remittances under the Liberalized Remittance Scheme, and overseas tour packages. The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 further extends TCS on sales of notified luxury goods (see Para 8.16). Under the pre-amended provisions of Section 192, TCS was not considered while calculating TDS on salary income, resulting in excess tax deduction from the salary income and eventually blocking employees' cash flow.

Similarly, in non-income TDS sections like Section 194N, where no income is generated for the assessee, Section 192 does not allow credit for the same in the TDS calculation on salary income. Consequently, all these TDS and TCS amounts are claimed as refunds in the income tax return, leading to increased interest costs for the department.

8.2-2b What all TDS and TCS shall be considered? - Section 192(2B) enables employers to consider all taxes deducted or collected under the Income Tax Act when calculating an employee's TDS liability. This includes tax deducted at source under sections 193 to 196D and tax collected at source under Sections 206C.

8.2-2c Which income or loss can be declared to the employer? – The employees can declare any income chargeable under any other head of income to the employer. However, only the loss under the head of income from house property can be declared to the employer. Any loss under other heads of income (e.g., business losses, capital losses) shall not be considered by the employers even if declared by the employees.

8.2-2d Is it necessary to declare the corresponding income for which the TDS is declared? – Section 192 does not explicitly specify whether an employee must also inform his employer about the corresponding income or transactions on which TDS/TCS has been deducted. If he declares only TDS/TCS but does not declare the corresponding income, there will be a deficit in his final tax liability and tax deducted under Section 192. Thus, it is apprehended that the Board may include fields in the form to be specified to report the corresponding income. This would be similar to the TDS schedule in the ITR forms, where the assessee needs to provide details of the TDS amount, the corresponding income, and the specific head under which this income is declared in the ITR.

RULE 134*

Application under section 155(20) regarding credit of tax deduction at source

Statutory background

134.1 The Finance Act, 2023 has inserted sub-section (20) to section 155 with effect from 1-10-2023. This new sub-section shall apply when an income has been reported in an income tax return u/s. 139 for a specific assessment year, and tax was withheld by the deductor and paid to the Central Government in a later financial year.

This situation arises when a deductor withholds tax in the year in which the income is paid to the taxpayer. However, the taxpayer has already included that income on an accrual basis in his earlier tax returns. This causes a TDS mismatch, as the income has already been taxed on accrual basis, but tax is only deducted later when payment is made. The taxpayer cannot claim TDS credit in the year in which it was deducted because the income was not taxed in that year. It may also be too late to revise the past income tax return in which the income was reported, as the time limit to do so may have expired. This creates a problem for the taxpayer in claiming TDS credit.

Section 155(20) enables the assessee to make an application in the Form prescribed under Rule 134 (see para 134.2) to the AO within a period of 2 years from the end of the financial year in which the tax was withheld, and the AO will amend the assessment and allow credit for the tax. The provisions of section 154 will also apply, and the four year limit to amend the assessment order or the intimation will be counted from the financial year in which tax was withheld. It should be noted that the credit for the tax will not be allowed in any other assessment year.

11.8 Person deemed to be assessee in default

Section 201 of the Act provides that where any person including principal officer of a company required to deduct any tax, (hereinafter collectively referred as 'person responsible') does not deduct or does not pay or after deducting fails to pay, the whole or any part of the tax, he is deemed to be 'an assessee in default in respect of such tax' (hereafter referred as 'Assessee in default'). The Supreme Court in Hindustan Coca Cola Beverage (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2007] 163 Taxman 355/ 293 ITR 226 upheld the decision of Tribunal that if the tax is paid by the payee, the shortfall in deduction of tax cannot be reco-vered from the payer or the deductor.

11.8.1 Amendment

Finance Act, 2012 inserts first proviso in sub-section (1), with effect from 1-7-2012 to provide that in certain circumstances person responsible shall not be deemed to be assessee in default.

Person responsible, not to be regarded as assessee in default would be person responsible who fails to deduct the whole or any part of tax in accordance with the provisions of Chapter XVII-B from the amount cre-dited or paid to a resident, subject to fulfilment of the conditions.

11.8.2 Conditions

To enable person responsible to claim that he shall not be assessee in default, the following conditions need to be complied:

(a) The payee is a resident.

(b) The resident payee has furnished his return of income under section 139.

Where a payee does not furnish his return of income, benefit of the first proviso would not be available to person responsible.

Return must be furnished under section 139 implying that any delayed or revised return would satisfy the condition. Any return other than under section 139 is not covered.

(c) The resident payee has included the amount paid or credited (without suffering TDS) for computing income in the return.

(d) The resident payee has paid the tax on income declared in the return furnished.

(e) Person responsible must furnish a certificate to this effect from an accountant in prescribed form.

The prescribed form would contain the details to be furnished. The details could be in relation to the conditions imposed, namely: furnishing of return; inclusion of the amount credited or paid on which tax is not deducted in the income returned; and tax is paid on such income.

An Explanation is inserted after section 201(4) to define 'accountant', having the same meaning as assigned to it in Explanation below section 288(2).

11.8.3 Analysis

11.8.3a Non-application of proviso

(a) Sub-section (1) deems person responsible as assessee in default, inter alia, in case of non-payment also. However, the proviso restricts its applicability to person responsible who has failed to deduct tax.

(b) It applies only in case of a payment to a resident. Accordingly, when payment or credit is made to a non-resident the proviso would not apply. In other words, in such a case, person responsible would be deemed to be assessee in default, as the first proviso will not apply.

11.8.3b Certificate - On reading the provision, it creates an impression that person responsible has to obtain and furnish certificate from accountant. However, since the details pertain to a resident payee, it appears that the resident payee will have to obtain the certificate and provide the same to person responsible to enable him to claim that he may not be consi-dered as assessee in default. However, a specific obligation is not cast on the resident payee. In absence thereof, Person responsible may have difficulties in obtaining and furnishing such certificate.

11.8.3c If payee is not required to file a return of income - In such a case, obviously, the conditions stipulated cannot be fulfilled. Hence, person responsible will not be able to comply with the requirement of furnishing certificate from accountant. In such a case, on a plain reading, and person the proviso would not apply responsible can be treated as assessee in default and all the consequences would follow.

11.8.3d Where the payee follows cash method of accounting - In a given case, person responsible fails to deduct tax at source, upon credit, say, in March 2012. The payee is following cash method of accounting and accounts the same in financial year 2012-13. The payee pays the tax thereon and files the return of income in June 2013 and also furnishes the certificate from Accountant, before due date of filing return of income, for assessment year 2013-14. In terms of the provisions, accounting year 2013-14 would be considered as the year of payment. The payment is made before the due date of filing return for assessment year 2013-14 and, hence, person responsible would be entitled to the deduction in computing the income of the previous year 2012-13 (relevant to assessment year 2013-14).

11.8.4 Amendment in section 206C

Section 206C requires collection of tax at source at the time of debiting amount to the buyer or receipt of such amount.

"... 3. Supreme Court in Hindustan Coca Cola Beverage (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2007] 163 Taxman 355/ 293 ITR 226, applying the above circular, accepted the contention that the tax cannot be recovered from the assessee.

4. Having regard to the above position in law, the tax could not have been recovered and accordingly, as such, the question of any payment by the deductor would not arise. In that case, the deductor would not be in a position to claim the expenditure as allowable, since they would not be in a position to fulfil the condition stipulated by section 40(a)(ia) of the Act. In other words, the deductor would suffer the loss, although, the tax is paid directly by the deductee. Obviously, this cannot be a position in law.

5. To remove the anomaly and/or hardships to the deductor, as explained in the Memorandum, the position in law is now clarified. For the purpose, certain procedural requirement is also introduced in the form of furnishing of a certificate from Accountant, as detailed above.

6. Thus, the amendment removes the defect and, hence, as held by Supreme Court in CIT v. Alom Extrusions Ltd. [2009] 185 Taxman 416/ 319 ITR 306 [following its earlier decisions in Allied Motors (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [1997] 91 Taxman 205/ 224 ITR 677 (SC) and CIT v. J.H. Gotla [1985] 23 Taxman 14J/ 156 ITR 323 (SC)], wherein it was observed (from headnotes) :

"When a proviso in a section is inserted to remedy unintended consequences and to make the section workable, the proviso which supplies an obvious omission therein is required to be read retrospectively in operation, particularly to give effect to the section as a whole. ... If strict construction leads to a result not intended to be subserved by the object of the legislation, and if another construction is possible apart from the literal construction, then that construction should be preferred".

7. Finance Act, 2010 substituted the first proviso to section 40(a)(ia), with effect from 1-4-2010, to provide that if the payment is made before the due date of filing of a return, the condition should be considered as fulfilled and accordingly the expenditure should be allowed. A question had arisen whether the proviso applied to any assessment year prior to assessment year 2010-11. Calcutta High Court has taken the view in CIT v. However, Special Bench of ITAT of Mumbai has taken a contrary view in Bharati Shipyard Limited v. Dy. CIT [2011] 132 ITD 53/ 13 taxmann.com 101, which, in any case, cannot apply to the provisions under consideration inasmuch as the Memorandum itself notes that the provision is made to clarify the matter and it is a beneficial provision.

for tax deduction at source [Section 155]

9.5 Under section 199, any deduction of tax at source in accordance with the provisions of sections 192 to 196D and paid to the account of Central Government is treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, and credit is given to such person for the amounts so deducted on the production of a certificate furnished under section 203 in the assessment year for which such income is assessable. In many cases certificates under section 203 are not furnished to the payee and as a result credit is not given for the tax so deducted.

With a view to mitigate this hardship, section 155(14), has been inserted, with effect from 1-6-2002, to provide that where in the assessment under section 143(3) or in any intimation or deemed intimation under section 143(1), credit for tax deducted has not been given under section 199 on the ground that the certificate furnished under section 203 was not filed with the return and subsequently such certificate is produced before the Assessing Officer within two years from the end of the assessment year in which such income is assessable, credit of tax deducted at source shall be given to the assessee on production of such certificate by rectification of the assessment order/intimation/deemed intimation. However, such rectification shall be made only if the income from which tax has been deducted has been disclosed in the return of income filed by the assessee for that assessment year [proviso to section 155(14)].

The time limit for rectification is 2 years from the end of the assessment year in which the income is assessable. Hence, in case of scrutiny assessments for which the same time limit is provided, the amendment does not provide any significant time for rectification after such assessment is complete.

Block assessment

9.6 The Finance Act, 1995 had introduced a new Chapter in the Act regarding New Scheme for assessment of Undisclosed Income (‘UnI’) determined as a result of search viz., ‘Chapter XIV-B - Special Procedure for Assessment of Search Cases’. The Finance Act, 2002 seeks to amend certain provisions of the said Chapter with retrospective effect from 1-7-1995. The Memorandum explaining provisions of the Finance (No. 2) Bill, 2002, classifies the amendments as rationalization of the provisions of Chapter XIV-B. It further clarifies that the amendments proposed are to remove inconsistencies in some of the provisions of block assessment and to rationalize the provisions.

The amendments made, in brief, are as under :—

◆ Section 158(b) defining UnI is amended to include therein any expense, deduction or allowance claimed but found to be false. (see para 9.6-1)

◆ Section 158BB(1) providing for the computation of UnI is amended to provide that such income is to be computed on the basis of evidence found as a result of search and materials or information available with Assessing Officer that is ‘relatable to such evidence’. (see para 9.6-3)

◆ Clause (a) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that assessed income to be reduced from the total income of the block period to determine UnI shall be that income, the assessment of which is concluded prior to the date of commencement of the search or the date of requisition.

◆ Similarly clause (b) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that returned income which is to be reduced to determine UnI shall include even the income as per the returns filed pursuant to notice under section 142(1)/148. (see para 9.6-2b)

◆ Clause (c) to section 158BB(1) is substituted by a new clause which seeks to cover those cases separately where returns are not filed by the assessee and as per the entries as recorded in books of account maintained in the normal course :

- results either into a loss; or

- income does not exceed the maximum amount not chargeable to tax. (see para 9.6-2b)

◆ Explanation (a) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that total income of each previous year in the block period shall be computed as per the Act, as against the earlier provision which provided that it shall be computed as per Chapter IV. (see para 9.6-2a)

◆ Section 158BC of the Act is amended to provide that provisions of section 145 will also apply for determining the UnI. (see para 9.6-4)

◆ All the above amendments are made retrospectively with effect from 1-7-1995.

◆ Clause (d) of section 158BC is amended to provide that the assets seized or requisitioned shall be dealt with in accordance with the newly substituted section 132B of the Act. (see para 9.6-5). This amendment is with effect from 1-6-2002.

Section 203

Finance Act, 2008

Dematerialisation of TDS and TCS certificates [Sections 203 & 206C]

8.6 An assessee is entitled to credit in respect of tax deducted at source ('TDS') and tax collected at source ('TCS') on the basis of a certificate issued by the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source. Such certificate has to be enclosed with the return of income to claim the credit.

The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004 proposed dematerialisation of TDS and TCS certificates and, inter alia1, provided that on and after 1-4-2005:

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source should file quarterly statements with the income-tax authority or authorised person;

such authority or person would furnish a statement of tax deducted or collected at source ('the Statement') to the payee or buyer;

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source need not furnish certificate to the payee or buyer; and

the payee or buyer would be entitled to the credit for TDS or TCS based on the statement furnished by such authority or person.

The Finance Act, 2005 postponed the implementation of the above by a year and the Finance Act, 2006 further postponed it up to 31-3-2008.

Pending stabilisation of the system, the Finance Act, 2008 has amended with effect from 1-4-2008, the following provisions to provide that the amendments made therein by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004, as further amended by the Finance Act, 2005 and Finance Act, 2006 would become effective from 1-4-2010 instead of 1-4-2008 as provided heretobefore:

Section 203(3) of the Act providing that a payer need not issue a certificate of TDS;

First proviso to section 206C(5) providing that a person responsible for collecting tax at source need not issue a certificate of TCS.

Further, the Explanation below section 139(9) providing that if the proof of tax deducted or collected at source is not attached on or after 1-4-2008, the return would not be considered as defective has been amended by deleting the words 'on or after 1st April, 2008'.

8.6-1 Analysis of amendments - The effect of the above amendments is as follows:

the credit for TDS or TCS, in respect of the financial years 2008-09 and 2009-10 (assessment years 2009-10 and 2010-11) will be available on the basis of certificates issued by the payer or the person responsible for collecting tax at source; and

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source will have to continue to issue certificates to the payee or the buyer, in respect of the tax deducted or collected at source during the financial years 2008-09 and 2009-10.

Section 203AA of the Act provides that the prescribed authority shall furnish the statement of TDS in the prescribed form and specifying prescribed particulars. Similarly, the second proviso of section 206C(5) provides that the prescribed authority shall furnish such statement of TCS. The Finance Act, 2006 had postponed the applicability of these provisions to the financial year beginning on or after 1-4-2008. Now, no amendment has been made to these provisions by the Finance Act, 2008.

◆ The completeness/accuracy of the Statement would depend on the timeliness and quality of the quarterly statements. ◆ The prescribed income-tax authority or the authorised agency has to deliver the Statement to the payee/buyer. There is no requirement about furnishing a copy of the Statement to the Assessing Officer of the payee/buyer.

◆ The Statement, in respect of TDS, should specify the amount of tax deducted or paid [under section 192(1A)] and other particulars as may be prescribed. Thus, the Statement would contain details of the tax deducted as per the provisions of the Chapter and paid under section 192(1A).

◆ The Statement, in respect of TCS, should specify the amount of tax collected.

◆ Thus, it may be noted that the Statement must specify:

■ TDS Statement:

● Amount of tax deducted as per the provisions of the Chapter; and/or

● Amount of tax paid under section 192(1A); and/or

● Such other particulars as may be prescribed.

■ TCS Statement:

● Amount of tax collected; and/or

● Such other particulars as may be prescribed.

◆ It may be noted that no provision has been made to provide for any deterrent for not furnishing the Statement or for not furnishing the same within the time prescribed. Further, there is no provision for the recourse, which the payee or buyer may have in such circumstances.

8.4-5 Credit for the tax deducted or collected - The provision in relation to :—

◆ TDS [section 199(3)], reads as follows: “where any deduction is made. . . on or after the 1st day of April, 2005 and paid to the Central Government, the amount of tax deducted and specified in the statement referred to in section 203AA shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the person referred to in sub-section (1) . . . and credit shall be given to him for the amount so deducted in the assessment... without production of certificate.” (Emphasis supplied)

◆ TCS [first proviso to section 206C(4)] reads: “provided that where any amount is collected... on or after 1st day of April, 2005 and paid... to the credit of the Central Government, the amount of tax collected and specified in statement referred to... shall be deemed as payment of tax on behalf of the person from whom the amount has been collected and credit shall be given to him for the amount so collected in the assessment... without production of certificate.” (Emphasis supplied)

Thus, the amount of tax deducted/collected and specified in the Statement would be treated as tax paid on behalf of the payee/buyer. It appears, the payee/buyer would get credit for such tax deducted/collected on his/her behalf. For whatever reasons, the amount of tax deducted/collected is not specified in the Statement, the amount not specified would not be treated as tax deducted/collected on behalf of the payee/buyer and credit will not be available for the same to the payee/buyer.

In this connection an issue may arise about the treatment of tax deducted or collected and specified in the statement but not paid by the payer/collector. If appears that to the extent tax deducted/collected, whether specified in the statement or not the recovery cannot be enforced against the payee/buyer, for the following reasons :

(i) Section 203AA and second proviso to section 206C(5), respectively provide that the prescribed income-tax authorities or authorised person shall prepare and collect the statement of tax deducted/paid [under section 192(1A)] on tax collected.

(ii) Section 199(3) and first proviso to section 206C(4) treat the tax deducted or collected and specified in the statement as tax paid on behalf of the payee or buyer. Thus, the tax deducted on collected, whether paid or not is the relevant amount which can be considered as paid on behalf of the payee/buyer.

(iii) Section 205 of the Act provides that where the tax is deductible at source under applicable provisions of Chapter XVII, the assessee shall not be called upon to pay the tax to the extent to which tax has been deducted from that income.

(iv) Section 191 contemplates direct payment by the payee only in a case where tax is deducted in terms of Chapter XVII and not in a case where the tax is deducted and not paid.

Finance Act, 2002

Amendment of rectification provisions for credit for tax deduction at source [Section 155]

9.5 Under section 199, any deduction of tax at source in accordance with the provisions of sections 192 to 196D and paid to the account of Central Government is treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, and credit is given to such person for the amounts so deducted on the production of a certificate furnished under section 203 in the assessment year for which such income is assessable.

In many cases certificates under section 203 are not furnished to the payee and as a result credit is not given for the tax so deducted.

With a view to mitigate this hardship, section 155(14), has been inserted, with effect from 1-6-2002, to provide that where in the assessment under section 143(3) or in any intimation or deemed intimation under section 143(1), credit for tax deducted has not been given under section 199 on the ground that the certificate furnished under section 203 was not filed with the return and subsequently such certificate is produced before the Assessing Officer within two years from the end of the assessment year in which such income is assessable, credit of tax deducted at source shall be given to the assessee on production of such certificate by rectification of the assessment order/intimation/deemed intimation. However, such rectification shall be made only if the income from which tax has been deducted has been disclosed in the return of income filed by the assessee for that assessment year [proviso to section 155(14)].

The time limit for rectification is 2 years from the end of the assessment year in which the income is assessable. Hence, in case of scrutiny assessments for which the same time limit is provided, the amendment does not provide any significant time for rectification after such assessment is complete.

The Finance Act, 2008 has substituted, with effect from 1-4-2008, the aforesaid section as follows :

◆ Sub-section (1) provides that any deduction made in accordance with Chapter XVII and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, or of the owner of the security, or of the depositor or of the owner of property or of the unitholder, or of the shareholder, as the case may be.

◆ Sub-section (2) provides that any sum referred to in section 192(1A) and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as the tax paid on behalf of the person in respect of whose income such payment of tax has been made.

◆ Sub-section (3) provides that the Board may, for the purposes of giving credit in respect of tax deducted or tax paid in terms of the provisions of this Chapter, make the following rules:

(a) rules for the purposes of giving credit to a person other than those referred to in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2),

(b) rules for the assessment year for which such credit may be given, and

(c) such other rules as may be necessary.

Thus, the gist of the amendment is that (a) the power to give credit to a person other than the person in whose name deduction has been made is now given to the Board instead of stating such instances in the Act itself; and (b) the Board will now also have the power to prescribe rules for the assessment year for which the credit of tax may be given and the manner in which such credit shall be given.

Section 199

Finance Act, 2008

Credit for tax deducted at source - Amendment to section 199 regarding credit for tax deducted

8.4 Section 199, prior to the amendment by the Finance Act, 2008, provided that any deduction of tax at source made under Chapter XVII and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, or of the owner of the security, or depositor or owner of property or of a unit holder or the shareholder, as the case may be. It was provided that credit shall be given to such person for the amount so deducted on the production of the certificate furnished under section 203 and such credit would be given in the assessment for the assessment year in which such income is assessable. The provisos to section 199(1) provided that

in cases where certain income was included in the total income of a person under section 60 (transfer of income without transfer of asset), section 61 (revocable transfer), section 64 (clubbing), section 93 (transfer of income of non-residents), section 94 (transactions in securities), the credit shall be given to the person in whose hands such income is taxable;

In case dividend income was assessable as an income of a person other than the shareholders, the credit shall be given to such other person in such circumstances as may be prescribed; and

If a property or asset is owned jointly by two or more persons not constituting a partnership, the credit shall be given to each such person in the same proportion in which such income is assessable as his income.

Section 199(2) provided that any tax paid under section 192(1A) shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the employee and credit shall be given to him for the amount so deducted on the production of the certificate under section 203 in the assessment year in which such income is assessable.

Section 199(3) provided that in respect of any tax deduction made on or after 1-4-2008 and paid to the Central Government, the amount of tax deducted and specified in the statement referred to in section 203AA shall be treated as tax paid on behalf of the persons referred to in section 199(1)/(2) and credit shall be given to him for the amounts so deducted in the assessment for which income is assessable without the production of certificates.

The Finance Act, 2008 has substituted, with effect from 1-4-2008, the aforesaid section as follows :

Sub-section (1) provides that any deduction made in accordance with Chapter XVII and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, or of the owner of the security, or of the depositor or of the owner of property or of the unitholder, or of the shareholder, as the case may be.

Sub-section (2) provides that any sum referred to in section 192(1A) and paid to the Central Government shall be treated as the tax paid on behalf of the person in respect of whose income such payment of tax has been made.

Sub-section (3) provides that the Board may, for the purposes of giving credit in respect of tax deducted or tax paid in terms of the provisions of this Chapter, make the following rules:

(a)

rules for the purposes of giving credit to a person other than those referred to in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2),

(b)

rules for the assessment year for which such credit may be given, and

(c)

such other rules as may be necessary.

Thus, the gist of the amendment is that (a) the power to give credit to a person other than the person in whose name deduction has been made is now given to the Board instead of stating such instances in the Act itself; and (b) the Board will now also have the power to prescribe rules for the assessment year for which the credit of tax may be given and the manner in which such credit shall be given.

for tax deduction at source [Section 155]

9.5 Under section 199, any deduction of tax at source in accordance with the provisions of sections 192 to 196D and paid to the account of Central Government is treated as a payment of tax on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made, and credit is given to such person for the amounts so deducted on the production of a certificate furnished under section 203 in the assessment year for which such income is assessable. In many cases certificates under section 203 are not furnished to the payee and as a result credit is not given for the tax so deducted.

With a view to mitigate this hardship, section 155(14), has been inserted, with effect from 1-6-2002, to provide that where in the assessment under section 143(3) or in any intimation or deemed intimation under section 143(1), credit for tax deducted has not been given under section 199 on the ground that the certificate furnished under section 203 was not filed with the return and subsequently such certificate is produced before the Assessing Officer within two years from the end of the assessment year in which such income is assessable, credit of tax deducted at source shall be given to the assessee on production of such certificate by rectification of the assessment order/intimation/deemed intimation. However, such rectification shall be made only if the income from which tax has been deducted has been disclosed in the return of income filed by the assessee for that assessment year [proviso to section 155(14)].

The time limit for rectification is 2 years from the end of the assessment year in which the income is assessable. Hence, in case of scrutiny assessments for which the same time limit is provided, the amendment does not provide any significant time for rectification after such assessment is complete.

Block assessment

9.6 The Finance Act, 1995 had introduced a new Chapter in the Act regarding New Scheme for assessment of Undisclosed Income (‘UnI’) determined as a result of search viz., ‘Chapter XIV-B - Special Procedure for Assessment of Search Cases’. The Finance Act, 2002 seeks to amend certain provisions of the said Chapter with retrospective effect from 1-7-1995. The Memorandum explaining provisions of the Finance (No. 2) Bill, 2002, classifies the amendments as rationalization of the provisions of Chapter XIV-B. It further clarifies that the amendments proposed are to remove inconsistencies in some of the provisions of block assessment and to rationalize the provisions.

The amendments made, in brief, are as under :—

◆ Section 158(b) defining UnI is amended to include therein any expense, deduction or allowance claimed but found to be false. (see para 9.6-1)

◆ Section 158BB(1) providing for the computation of UnI is amended to provide that such income is to be computed on the basis of evidence found as a result of search and materials or information available with Assessing Officer that is ‘relatable to such evidence’. (see para 9.6-3)

◆ Clause (a) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that assessed income to be reduced from the total income of the block period to determine UnI shall be that income, the assessment of which is concluded prior to the date of commencement of the search or the date of requisition.

◆ Similarly clause (b) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that returned income which is to be reduced to determine UnI shall include even the income as per the returns filed pursuant to notice under section 142(1)/148. (see para 9.6-2b)

◆ Clause (c) to section 158BB(1) is substituted by a new clause which seeks to cover those cases separately where returns are not filed by the assessee and as per the entries as recorded in books of account maintained in the normal course :

- results either into a loss; or

- income does not exceed the maximum amount not chargeable to tax. (see para 9.6-2b)

◆ Explanation (a) to section 158BB(1) is amended to provide that total income of each previous year in the block period shall be computed as per the Act, as against the earlier provision which provided that it shall be computed as per Chapter IV. (see para 9.6-2a)

◆ Section 158BC of the Act is amended to provide that provisions of section 145 will also apply for determining the UnI. (see para 9.6-4)

◆ All the above amendments are made retrospectively with effect from 1-7-1995.

◆ Clause (d) of section 158BC is amended to provide that the assets seized or requisitioned shall be dealt with in accordance with the newly substituted section 132B of the Act. (see para 9.6-5). This amendment is with effect from 1-6-2002.

Credit for TCS, where certificates are not filed, through rectification

8.3 Section 155(14) of the Act provides for rectification of assessment or intimation where credit for TDS has not been given on the ground that TDS certificate was not filed with the return and if the assessee produces such certificate before the Assessing Officer (‘AO’) within two years from end of assessment year in which such income is assessable, AO can rectify the order and allow the credit. One of the conditions, as stipulated by the proviso thereto, is that the income must have been disclosed in the return of income filed by the assessee for the relevant assessment year.

Similar relief or benefit was not available in a case where TCS certificate was not filed.

To extend similar relief or benefit to TCS credit, the Finance Act, 2006 has amended section 155 of the Act, with effect from 1-4-2007.

Accordingly, in a case where credit for TCS is not given since certificate has not been furnished along with the return and if the assessee produces the same within two years from the end of the assessment year in which the income was assessable, the assessee can claim credit thereof in rectification proceedings, provided the income has been disclosed in the return of income.

Interest payment on self-assessment basis

8.4 Section 201(1A) provides for payment of simple interest at 12% p.a., where the tax is not deducted, wholly or partly, or after deduction has not been paid, on the amount of such tax from the date on which such tax was deductible to the date on which such tax is actually paid.

In order to mandate payment of interest on self-assessment basis, the Finance Act, 2006 has amended sub-section (1A) to provide that such interest shall be paid before furnishing quarterly statement for each quarter in accordance with section 200(3) of the Act, with effect from 1-6-2006.

Similarly section 206C(7) of the Act provides for payment of interest in case of failure to collect the tax or after collecting, failure to pay the same.

The Finance Act, 2006 has also amended sub-section (7) to provide for payment of interest before furnishing the quarterly statement in accordance with section 206C(3) of the Act, with effect from 1-6-2006.

12.5-2m Whether tax is deductible on GST component? - The CBDT has clarified by issuing Circulars from time to time that tax is not required to be deducted on Service tax/GST component [Circular No. 4/2008, dated 28-4-2008, Circular No. 1/2014, dated 13-1-2014, Circular No.23/2017 dated 19-7-2017]. Hence, it can be said that tax is not required to be deducted on GST component, if the amount of consideration and GST are separately reflected in the Tax invoice.

12.5-2n Credit of TDS - When? - As per the provision of section 198(1), tax deducted in accordance with Chapter XVII-B is treated as deemed income of the payee or the recipient. Section 199(1) provides that tax deducted under the Chapter XVII-B would be treated as payment of tax on behalf of the payee. Further, rule 37BA(3)(i) provides that the credit of such TDS shall be given for the assessment year in which such income is assessable.

Thus, credit of TDS deducted under the section would be available only in the year in which the income is offered to tax by the payee. It may take time to complete work. Therefore, in order to avoid hardship of getting tax credit in future, it is advisable that the payee should:

keep and preserve the TDS certificate(s) issued by the tax deductor; or

keep tracking records of Form 26AS on Government website; or

12.6 Cash withdrawals and deduction of tax by banking company and others [Section 194N]

Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 inserts a new provision, namely, section 194N, in Chapter XVII-B, to provide for "TDS on cash withdrawal to discourage cash transactions", with effect from 1-9-2019.

In the Memorandum reasons for the provision, as explained, are:

"In order to further discourage cash transactions and move towards less cash economy it is proposed … to provide for levy of TDS at the rate of 2% on cash payments in excess of one crore rupees in aggregate made during the year, by a banking company or cooperative bank or post office, to any person from an account maintained by the recipient". (Emphasis supplied)

12.6-1 The provision

It provides as follows:

every person being:

a banking company [to which the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 applies (including a bank or banking institution referred to in section 51)];

a co-operative society engaged in carrying on business of banking; and

a post office,

is obliged to deduct tax (hereafter the above persons are collectively referred as "the banker");

the banker must be responsible for paying any sum or aggregate sums, in cash, in excess of Rs. 1 crore, during a previous year;

such payment must be made to any person ("the recipient") from one or more accounts maintained by the recipient with the banker;

the banker shall deduct 2% of the sum exceeding Rs. 1 crore, as income tax; and

the tax must be deducted at the time of the payment to the recipient in cash.

12.6-1a Excluded Payment - It is further provided by proviso to section 194N that the provision would not apply to any payment made to:

Government,

any banking company,

any co-operative society engaged in carrying on banking business,

post office,

any business correspondent of a banking company or a co-operative society engaged in banking business, in accordance with guidelines issued in this regard by the RBI,

Section 203

Finance Act, 2008

Dematerialisation of TDS and TCS certificates [Sections 203 & 206C]

8.6 An assessee is entitled to credit in respect of tax deducted at source ('TDS') and tax collected at source ('TCS') on the basis of a certificate issued by the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source. Such certificate has to be enclosed with the return of income to claim the credit.

The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004 proposed dematerialisation of TDS and TCS certificates and, inter alia1, provided that on and after 1-4-2005:

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source should file quarterly statements with the income-tax authority or authorised person;

such authority or person would furnish a statement of tax deducted or collected at source ('the Statement') to the payee or buyer;

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source need not furnish certificate to the payee or buyer; and

the payee or buyer would be entitled to the credit for TDS or TCS based on the statement furnished by such authority or person.

The Finance Act, 2005 postponed the implementation of the above by a year and the Finance Act, 2006 further postponed it up to 31-3-2008.

Pending stabilisation of the system, the Finance Act, 2008 has amended with effect from 1-4-2008, the following provisions to provide that the amendments made therein by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004, as further amended by the Finance Act, 2005 and Finance Act, 2006 would become effective from 1-4-2010 instead of 1-4-2008 as provided heretobefore:

Section 203(3) of the Act providing that a payer need not issue a certificate of TDS;

First proviso to section 206C(5) providing that a person responsible for collecting tax at source need not issue a certificate of TCS.

Further, the Explanation below section 139(9) providing that if the proof of tax deducted or collected at source is not attached on or after 1-4-2008, the return would not be considered as defective has been amended by deleting the words 'on or after 1st April, 2008'.

8.6-1 Analysis of amendments - The effect of the above amendments is as follows:

the credit for TDS or TCS, in respect of the financial years 2008-09 and 2009-10 (assessment years 2009-10 and 2010-11) will be available on the basis of certificates issued by the payer or the person responsible for collecting tax at source; and

the person responsible for deducting or collecting tax at source will have to continue to issue certificates to the payee or the buyer, in respect of the tax deducted or collected at source during the financial years 2008-09 and 2009-10.

Section 203AA of the Act provides that the prescribed authority shall furnish the statement of TDS in the prescribed form and specifying prescribed particulars. Similarly, the second proviso of section 206C(5) provides that the prescribed authority shall furnish such statement of TCS. The Finance Act, 2006 had postponed the applicability of these provisions to the financial year beginning on or after 1-4-2008. Now, no amendment has been made to these provisions by the Finance Act, 2008.

11.8 Person deemed to be assessee in default

Section 201 of the Act provides that where any person including principal officer of a company required to deduct any tax, (hereinafter collectively referred as 'person responsible') does not deduct or does not pay or after deducting fails to pay, the whole or any part of the tax, he is deemed to be 'an assessee in default in respect of such tax' (hereafter referred as 'Assessee in default'). The Supreme Court in Hindustan Coca Cola Beverage (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2007] 163 Taxman 355/ 293 ITR 226 upheld the decision of Tribunal that if the tax is paid by the payee, the shortfall in deduction of tax cannot be reco-vered from the payer or the deductor.

11.8.1 Amendment

Finance Act, 2012 inserts first proviso in sub-section (1), with effect from 1-7-2012 to provide that in certain circumstances person responsible shall not be deemed to be assessee in default.

Person responsible, not to be regarded as assessee in default would be person responsible who fails to deduct the whole or any part of tax in accordance with the provisions of Chapter XVII-B from the amount cre-dited or paid to a resident, subject to fulfilment of the conditions.

11.8.2 Conditions

To enable person responsible to claim that he shall not be assessee in default, the following conditions need to be complied:

(a) The payee is a resident.

(b) The resident payee has furnished his return of income under section 139.

Where a payee does not furnish his return of income, benefit of the first proviso would not be available to person responsible.

Return must be furnished under section 139 implying that any delayed or revised return would satisfy the condition. Any return other than under section 139 is not covered.

(c) The resident payee has included the amount paid or credited (without suffering TDS) for computing income in the return.

(d) The resident payee has paid the tax on income declared in the return furnished.

(e) Person responsible must furnish a certificate to this effect from an accountant in prescribed form.

The prescribed form would contain the details to be furnished. The details could be in relation to the conditions imposed, namely: furnishing of return; inclusion of the amount credited or paid on which tax is not deducted in the income returned; and tax is paid on such income.

An Explanation is inserted after section 201(4) to define 'accountant', having the same meaning as assigned to it in Explanation below section 288(2).

11.8.3 Analysis

11.8.3a Non-application of proviso

(a) Sub-section (1) deems person responsible as assessee in default, inter alia, in case of non-payment also. However, the proviso restricts its applicability to person responsible who has failed to deduct tax.

(b) It applies only in case of a payment to a resident. Accordingly, when payment or credit is made to a non-resident the proviso would not apply. In other words, in such a case, person responsible would be deemed to be assessee in default, as the first proviso will not apply.

11.8.3b Certificate - On reading the provision, it creates an impression that person responsible has to obtain and furnish certificate from accountant. However, since the details pertain to a resident payee, it appears that the resident payee will have to obtain the certificate and provide the same to person responsible to enable him to claim that he may not be consi-dered as assessee in default. However, a specific obligation is not cast on the resident payee. In absence thereof, Person responsible may have difficulties in obtaining and furnishing such certificate.

11.8.3c If payee is not required to file a return of income - In such a case, obviously, the conditions stipulated cannot be fulfilled. Hence, person responsible will not be able to comply with the requirement of furnishing certificate from accountant. In such a case, on a plain reading, and person the proviso would not apply responsible can be treated as assessee in default and all the consequences would follow.

11.8.3d Where the payee follows cash method of accounting - In a given case, person responsible fails to deduct tax at source, upon credit, say, in March 2012. The payee is following cash method of accounting and accounts the same in financial year 2012-13. The payee pays the tax thereon and files the return of income in June 2013 and also furnishes the certificate from Accountant, before due date of filing return of income, for assessment year 2013-14. In terms of the provisions, accounting year 2013-14 would be considered as the year of payment. The payment is made before the due date of filing return for assessment year 2013-14 and, hence, person responsible would be entitled to the deduction in computing the income of the previous year 2012-13 (relevant to assessment year 2013-14).

11.8.4 Amendment in section 206C

Section 206C requires collection of tax at source at the time of debiting amount to the buyer or receipt of such amount.
